subject: Next steps: On-prem air-gapped deployment details — HW, upgrades, and offline ops
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Weber <tom.weber@legacybank.com>
Cc: Anita Rao <anita.rao@legacybank.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: On-prem air-gapped deployment details — HW, upgrades, and offline ops

Hi Tom / Anita,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — great to hear more about LegacyBank's requirements. Per our call, below is a concise recap and proposed next steps so we can validate whether Private (on-prem air-gapped) is the right fit vs Dedicated:

Recap:
- Workload: customer support and document understanding pipelines, peak concurrency ~120 sessions, avg seq len 1k tokens.
- Security: fully offline, no egress allowed from inference hosts; key material managed by customer HSM.
- Ops constraints: limited maintenance windows (weekly 2-hour window), strict change freeze during business hours.
- Desired SLOs: p95 latency < 350ms for short prompts, throughput to handle sustained bursts.

Questions / open items (for validation):
1) Hardware baseline: do you have a preference for vendor (Dell/HPE) and GPUs? We typically recommend 8x A100-40GB for initial clusters, or 4x H100 for performance-sensitive workloads. See attached baseline spec.
2) Offline upgrades: how should we schedule kernel/model upgrades for air-gapped hosts? Do you have a staging cluster accessible, or will upgrades be done through removable media?
3) Network topology: we need switch-level diagrams and jump-box access policy for private packaging. Can you share a network diagram and firewall rules?

Next steps:
- Please confirm the two items above and attach any network diagrams or current hardware list.
- I'll loop in our infra engineer (Dev Patel) and product lead (Lauren Bishop) to draft an air-gapped runbook and a hardware checklist.

Attachments: LegacyBank-HW-reqs.pdf (baseline spec)

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
m: 555-10102

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the follow up and summary — that aligns with our thinking. A few clarifications:

- Hardware: we're currently evaluating Dell r750 with up to 4x H100s per chassis. We're open to 8x 40GB A100 if that gives better density/cost. Do you have a recommendation on the tradeoff for model sizes we discussed (7B vs 13B)?
- Upgrades: due to policy we have two options: (A) upgrades via removable media administered by our infra team during a weekly window, or (B) staged cluster in an isolated lab that can be connected briefly for patching. Option A is preferred but slower.
- Network: I'll attach a simplistic network diagram; full design can be shared after an NDA addendum if needed.

Also, curious on offline monitoring — do you have a way to stream metrics from air-gapped hosts to our on-prem monitoring without egress?

I'll attach the initial network sketched diagram. Looping in Anita for procurement timelines — we're aiming for a procurement decision by end of Q2.

Best,
Tom

Marissa,

Thanks for the context — see answers inline and a recommended starting configuration below.

Summary recommendations:
- Baseline: 4x H100 (80GB) per chassis x 3 chassis (12 GPUs) to start; gives room for 13B models with batching and reaches target p95 latency under expected concurrency. If procurement prefers density, 8x A100-40GB per chassis x 2 chassis could be an alternative (better per-GPU cost, higher orchestration overhead).
- Storage: NVMe local per host + NFS for model blobs (air-gapped transfer via signed dbars). Ensure at least 4TB usable NVMe per host.
- Offline upgrades: we support removable media updates. Our runbook will include:
  - Signed bundle creation and sha256 checksums
  - Verification steps on isolated staging node
  - Staged rollout in maintenance windows with automatic rollback on health checks
- Monitoring: push metrics to a local Prometheus instance; we can export periodic snapshots (tar.gz) that your team pulls via removable media, or use an inbound "pull box" that we can ship to you for collection (no outbound connections required).

Attachments: Network-Diagram.png (annotated)
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cLEGACY-HW

I'll prepare the runbook and hardware checklist by EOD Wednesday and share a draft link. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call with your infra team.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
